title: Trump admin empowers private US firms to go after transnational cybercriminals
content_md: <p>The National Coordination Center will create a program allowing authorized U.S. companies to conduct cyber operations against transnational criminal organizations at the direction of the federal government, according to a <a href=“ Expanding Capabilities to Combat Transnational Cyber-Enabled Crime – The White House ”>memorandum</a> signed by President Donald Trump on Wednesday.&nbsp;</p> <p>Program executive directors from the departments of Homeland Security and Justice will have the authority to greenlight companies&rsquo; cyber operations unless the authorization would result in a loss of life, serious injury or &ldquo;rise to the level of use of forced or armed attack under international law.&rdquo;</p> <p>The federal government would vet and conduct oversight of authorized companies, which would need to enter into contractual agreements with either DHS or Justice.</p> <p>The specific standards the government will use to screen the companies will be drafted by the program executive directors &mdash; in coordination with the Homeland Security Council &mdash; within 60 days of the memo&rsquo;s signing.
